architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added decodeURIComponent() to parse URL-encoded cookie values before passing to URLSearchParams
architecture_decisions.rationale: Next.js's response.cookies.set() automatically URL-encodes cookie values containing special characters like '=' and '&'. The original implementation failed because URLSearchParams expects unencoded key-value pairs. By decoding first, we handle both encoded and unencoded formats transparently.
alternatives_considered: Using a custom parser instead of URLSearchParams
Accepting only unencoded values and requiring callers to decode

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Maintained backward compatibility by decoding all values, not just encoded ones
architecture_decisions.rationale: decodeURIComponent() safely passes through already-unencoded strings (it returns them unchanged). This ensures existing cookies continue to work while adding support for Next.js's encoded format. No conditional logic needed.
alternatives_considered: Detecting encoded vs unencoded and applying decodeURIComponent() conditionally
Creating two parsing paths for different cookie formats
Throwing errors for encoded cookies in old code

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added comprehensive test cases covering URL-encoded cookies in various scenarios
architecture_decisions.rationale: Tests verify: 1) Basic URL-encoded parsing works, 2) Different boolean flag combinations, 3) Cookie parsing among multiple cookies in header. This ensures the fix handles real-world Next.js production scenarios and edge cases.
alternatives_considered: Testing at integration level instead of unit level
Relying on existing tests without adding new ones

tickets.title: Fix URL-encoded cookie parsing for Next.js compatibility
tickets.description: Update mw_diag cookie parser to handle URL-encoded values produced by Next.js's response.cookies.set() method, which encodes special characters like '=' as %3D and '&' as %26

implementation_summary:
The change addresses a compatibility issue between the mw_diag cookie parser and Next.js's cookie handling. Next.js automatically URL-encodes cookie values when using response.cookies.set(), turning characters like '=' and '&' into %3D and %26 respectively. The original parser used URLSearchParams directly on the raw cookie value, which failed because URLSearchParams expects unencoded key-value pairs.

The fix is minimal and elegant: simply wrap the raw cookie value with decodeURIComponent() before passing it to URLSearchParams. This single-line change handles both encoded and unencoded formats transparently, since decodeURIComponent() returns unencoded strings unchanged. This maintains perfect backward compatibility while adding support for Next.js's production format.

The accompanying test additions are comprehensive, covering the exact encoded format Next.js produces, different boolean flag combinations, and the scenario where the mw_diag cookie appears among other cookies in the header. This ensures the parser works correctly in real-world deployment scenarios where cookies are set by Next.js middleware or API routes.
